keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Swabia row before the Hohenstaufen shape of 1260). The Duchy of Swabia page gives the extent 'from the Vosges in the west to the Lech in the east, and south to Chiavenna and the Gotthard Pass'; the Alsace page says Alsace 'was united with the other Alemanni east of the Rhine into the stem duchy of Swabia' without a year, so Alsace is included from the start at low confidence. The page gives no area; the gazetteer shape is about 70,000 km2 against Cliopatria's Hohenstaufen shape of 53,000 km2 for 1260 (ratio 0.75), so the extent is a generous reading. The Basel estates, which eu-08-a's Kingdom of Germany dossier records as going to Burgundy in 926, are left out. Alsace (thin finding, Alsace page opened): 'Alsace was united with the other Alemanni east of the Rhine into the stem duchy of Swabia', placed after the Treaty of Ribemont of 880 and given no year; the page is silent on 925-926 and on Basel in 926, and the Duchy of Swabia page never names Alsace but runs the duchy 'from the Alsatian Vosges mountain range in the west to the right bank of the river Lech in the east'. Alsace stays drawn from 915 at the dossier's reading; the Basel lands of 926 remain undrawn.

ledger.note: 915: Erchanger proclaims himself duke of Swabia. 'Duchy was proclaimed by the Ahalolfing count palatine Erchanger in 915' (infobox 'Proclaimed 915'); Erchanger and Burchard II had defeated Conrad I at Wahlwies. Count Burchard I, the Hunfriding, had been killed in 911. The extent is the page's description.

917: Burchard II becomes duke after Erchanger's execution. 'After Erchanger was executed on 21 January 917' Burchard 'seized all his lands and was recognised universally as duke'; the Duchy of Swabia page says Erchanger was executed on Conrad I's order.
919: King Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy seizes the county of Zürich. 'In 919, King Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy seized the county of Zürich.'

919: Burchard II defeats Rudolph II at Winterthur and Rudolph leaves Zürich. Burchard recognised the newly elected Henry the Fowler in the same year; in 922 he married his daughter Bertha to Rudolph and affirmed the peace (Burchard II page).
948: Hermann I dies and Otto the Great gives the duchy to his son Liudolf; the Ottonian house takes Swabia.
1038: Hermann IV dies and Henry (later Henry III) receives the duchy; the duchy is in the royal house's hands until 1045.

1079: the Hohenstaufen take the duchy. Rudolph of Rheinfelden, duke, was chosen German king against Henry IV in 1077 and Frederick I of Hohenstaufen received Swabia; 'Hohenstaufen hold the duchy, with a brief interruption, until 1268'.

1096: Frederick I cedes the Breisgau to Berthold II of Zähringen, the rival duke of 1092; in 1098 Berthold 'reconciled with Frederick, renounced all claims to Swabia' and became Duke of Zähringen (Zähringen page). Repair of 2026-10-25 (review): the Zähringen side dates the settlement 1098 (duchy-of-zahringen found 1098: Berthold 'reconciled with Frederick, renounced all claims to Swabia'), two years after the cession of 1096 that the Duchy of Swabia page dates; both years are the pages' own, the cession is kept at 1096, so the Breisgau is undrawn 1096-1097 (the Zähringen dossier was not touched).

1173: the Zähringer acquire Zürich. 'Zürich (acquired 1173)'; the Counts of Lenzburg shared the jurisdiction 'until 1173' (House of Zähringen page). The page is silent on whether Zürich had been Swabian and the Duchy of Swabia page is silent on 1173, so the year is the page's and the transfer from this duchy is the dossier's reading (confidence 2). Mirror of duchy-of-zahringen's 1173 gain, which names the Counts of Lenzburg as counterpart (not touched). Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

1198: Schaffhausen goes to the Zähringer. 'Schaffhausen (acquired 1198)' (House of Zähringen page); the Duchy of Swabia page says that in 1198 Philip 'purchased support by large cessions of Swabian lands' without naming them. Mirror of duchy-of-zahringen's 1198 gain (counterpart holy-roman-empire there; not touched). Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

1198: the Ortenau goes to the Zähringer (soft). The Duchy of Swabia page: Philip 'purchased support by large cessions of Swabian lands' in 1198, lands not named; the House of Zähringen page is silent on the Ortenau in 1198. The region is the circle duchy-of-zahringen draws; confidence 1. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

ledger.note: 1260: the dossier hands the duchy to house-of-hohenstaufen. The Duchy of Swabia page dates the end later: 'The duchy fell into abeyance after Conradin's death in 1268' (Conradin beheaded at Naples on 29 October 1268, Conradin page), and is silent on 1260, on Conrad IV's death in 1254 and on the interregnum; it adds that Conradin 'pledged his Swabian inheritance to Ulrich II, count of Württemberg' in 1266 (not drawn) and that the title was revived for the Habsburgs (infobox 1289). The year 1260 is the first year of Cliopatria's House of Hohenstaufen row (eu-09, 1260-1271, 50,823 km2), which draws the same duchy, so the dossier stops here to avoid drawing it twice; 1260-1268 belong to that dossier, which also carries the Conradin war. Confidence 1 for the year. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

wars.name: Conrad I's war against Erchanger and Burchard
wars.outcome: Erchanger and Burchard II defeated Conrad I at Wahlwies in 915; Erchanger was executed on Conrad's order on 21 January 917 and Burchard II became duke.

wars.name: Battle of Winterthur
wars.outcome: Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy seized the county of Zürich in 919 and was defeated by Burchard II at Winterthur; peace was affirmed in 922.

wars.name: Zähringen contest for Swabia
wars.outcome: Berthold II was elected duke of Swabia in 1092 against Frederick I; in 1096 Frederick ceded the Breisgau and in 1098 Berthold renounced Swabia and became Duke of Zähringen.
wars.note: No fighting zone is dated beyond the cession.

certainty.note: Stem-duchy frontiers (the Vosges, the Lech, the Gotthard) are descriptive; no treaty fixes them on the pages opened.

notes:
Five pages opened (budget 2-5). No capital is given (infobox lists none), so identity.capitals is empty; no complete list of dukes is on the pages (the extraction gave partial reigns), so no ruler strip. Cliopatria's only Swabian shape is House of Hohenstaufen 1260..1271 (50,823 km2), eu-09's. Not settled: Alsace's entry into Swabia (undated; Lotharingia held it before), Basel 926 (see kingdom-of-germany), when Baden separated, what the Zähringen held in Zürich (advocacy or ownership), and the 1266 pledge of the Swabian inheritance to Ulrich II of Württemberg (Conradin page silent; not drawn). Counterparts needing dossiers: Zähringen duchy (1098-1218, Breisgau, Zürich and the Burgundian rectorate) and Ulrich II of Württemberg's county.

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (0) the gazetteer region 'Swabia' (Baden-Württemberg plus an 80 km circle round Augsburg) is replaced everywhere by Baden-Württemberg plus Bayern west of the Lech (the polygon stem-duchy-of-bavaria now subtracts), because the circle reached Munich and so still overlapped Bavaria by 36 cells after Bavaria's own fix; the Duchy of Swabia page runs the duchy 'to the right bank of the river Lech', so a thin strip east of the river is not drawn. The Württemberg-Franken part of Baden-Württemberg still overlaps the gazetteer's Franconia circles (about 26 cells) in 915-939; stem-duchy-of-franconia (pass) was not touched. (1) the duchy ends in 1260, not 1268, and is handed to house-of-hohenstaufen (Cliopatria 1260-1271, eu-09) so that 1260-1268 is drawn once; the Duchy of Swabia page was re-read: abeyance after Conradin's death in 1268, silent on 1260 and on the interregnum; the Conradin war (1267-1268) is removed from wars[] because it lies outside the life 915-1260 and belongs to house-of-hohenstaufen (eu-09): belligerents house-of-hohenstaufen and kingdom-of-sicily; outcome: Conradin entered Rome in July 1268, lost at Tagliacozzo on 23 August 1268 and was beheaded at Naples on 29 October 1268, and the Swabian duchy lapsed; source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conradin. If the orchestrator prefers Swabia to run to 1268, the Hohenstaufen row's years must be trimmed instead. (2) Losses: Zürich in 1173, Schaffhausen and the Ortenau in 1198 (counterpart duchy-of-zahringen; keyframes 1173 and 1198); the House of Zähringen page gives 'Zürich (acquired 1173)' and 'Schaffhausen (acquired 1198)' and is silent on the Ortenau; the Duchy of Swabia page is silent on both and on 1173, and says only that Philip bought support with 'large cessions of Swabian lands' in 1198. The Zähringen dossier's counterparts for 1173 and 1198 are 'Counts of Lenzburg' and holy-roman-empire and should name stem-duchy-of-swabia (not touched). (3) The 1096 loss and the 1098 Zähringen found are two pages' own years; the cession stays at 1096, so the Breisgau is undrawn for two years. (4) Thin finding: the Alsace page says Alsace was united with the Alemanni into the stem duchy of Swabia after the Treaty of Ribemont (880), gives no year and is silent on 926 and Basel.
